title: Connect an AI assistant
summary: Let Claude Code, Claude or ChatGPT make courses for you, safely.
focus: The switch, tokens, plain HTTP and the least access
content:
## Let an assistant make courses

An AI assistant you already use, such as Claude Code, Claude or ChatGPT, can make and change your courses. It writes the lessons; Skrongle checks them and adds the course to your list. It never sees your progress or anyone else's courses.

The owner first turns on **Let apps connect** on **Manage Users**. An account needs the **Create courses** permission, so a Student account cannot connect an app.

## A token is a password

On your profile, under **Connected apps**, **Make a token** gives you a token. It is a password for making courses as you. It is shown once. Do not paste it into a chat, a screenshot or a shared file, and never put it in a web address. If in doubt, click **Revoke**.

## Choose the least

Tick only one course if the assistant needs only one. Choose **Read your courses** if it only looks. Choose **30 days** for a try-out.

## At home and through a domain

On a home network the address starts with http, so anyone who can read that network can copy a token. Do not use a token over public Wi-Fi. Claude and ChatGPT on the web connect from the internet, so they need a public https address and sign in with **Allow** instead of a token.

The docs page **Connect an AI assistant** has the steps.

the owner's switch on Manage Users that allows connected apps

options: A password for making courses as you
A public link to your course
quiz.correct_answer: A password for making courses as you
quiz.explanation: Whoever holds it can change your courses, so keep it to yourself.
hints: Think of what it lets someone do.

quiz.prompt: Where can you end an app's access?
options: Revoke, under Connected apps on your profile
quiz.correct_answer: Revoke, under Connected apps on your profile
quiz.explanation: Revoke stops the app at its next request.

quiz.prompt: It is fine to paste a token into a chat so the assistant can use it.
quiz.explanation: Never paste a token into a chat, a screenshot or a shared file, and never put it in a web address.

quiz.prompt: A Student account can connect an app.
quiz.explanation: Connecting an app needs the Create courses permission, which a Student does not have.
hints: Think of the permission it needs.

quiz.prompt: Which choice is the least access for a try-out that only needs to look at one course?
options: One course, Read your courses, 30 days
All courses, create and change, a year
No course ticked, create and change, 90 days
quiz.correct_answer: One course, Read your courses, 30 days
quiz.explanation: Give an app the fewest courses, the fewest rights and the shortest time.

sorts.title: Safe or not?

items.text: Revoke a token you are unsure about
Paste a token into a chat
Put a token in a web address
Use a token over public Wi-Fi

sorts.why: Keep a token to yourself, give it the least access, and revoke it if in doubt.
